Habor
HAY-bor
proper noun
Hebrew Chabor, from a root meaning to join or bind together; the river of Gozan in Assyria, a place of Israel’s captivity.

Biblical Definition

Habor was the river of Gozan in the land of Assyria whither the ten tribes were carried when Samaria fell: the king of Assyria “carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan” (2Ki 17:6). By this far stream the covenant curse came to its bitter fulfilment. Long before, in the law, the LORD had warned that if His people would not hearken He would scatter them among the heathen and draw out a sword after them; and now, by Habor’s waters, the sentence fell. The God of Israel Himself “stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria…and he carried them away” (1Ch 5:26) — not the arm of the heathen only, but the hand of a holy God chastening a people that forsook Him. Yet even in the place of exile the mercy of the covenant is not spent. He who passes His people through the waters is with them: “when thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee” (Isa 43:2). Habor teaches the dread seriousness of forsaking the LORD, for He will surely visit transgression with the rod; yet it teaches also that He preserves a remnant, and that no river of exile runs beyond the reach of His faithfulness.

Webster 1828 Definition

The river of Gozan in Assyria to which the ten tribes were carried captive (2Ki 17:6); a witness to the covenant curse of exile and to the LORD who yet preserves a remnant.

HABOR, the river of Gozan in the land of Assyria.

Thither the ten tribes of Israel were carried when Samaria fell.

The LORD Himself stirred up Assyria to carry His people away.

The exile fulfilled the covenant curse threatened in the law.

Yet He passes His people through the waters and preserves a remnant.

Key Scripture

2Ki 17:6 — "In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes."

1Ch 5:26 — "And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgathpilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river Gozan, unto this day."

Isa 43:2 — "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee."

Jer 2:13 — "For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water."

Modern Corruption

The river of Israel’s captivity; it recovers the seriousness of the covenant curse and the faithfulness of God to His remnant.

expand to see more

A river of the ancient captivity raises no fashionable dispute, and none is invented. Habor is named that we may feel both the terror and the mercy of the covenant.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD chastens the sin of His people in earnest — He carried the ten tribes to Habor by His own hand, that His threatenings are no idle words. Yet the same God is with His own even in the waters, and no river of exile overflows those He has chosen. Fear His rod, and rest in His faithfulness to preserve a remnant according to the election of grace.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Chabor, from a root meaning to join or bind; the river of Gozan in Assyria.

expand to see more

Habor — Hebrew Chabor, a river of Gozan (2Ki 17:6).

From a root signifying to join, unite, or bind together.

Named beside Halah as a place of Israel’s deportation.

A tributary within the region of Gozan in Mesopotamia.

Set in the record of the covenant curse executed upon the north.

Usage

"Israel was placed in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan."

"By Habor’s waters the covenant curse of exile was fulfilled."

"Habor teaches that God preserves a remnant even in captivity."
